metadata.title: Event-Driven Gateway Refresh for Pooled Sessions with Notifications
metadata.author: kevalmahajan

description:
# ✨ Feature / Enhancement PR

## 🔗 Epic / Issue

Closes #1984 

(Phase 2 of https://github.com/IBM/mcp-context-forge/issues/1984#issuecomment-3734591382)

---

## 🚀 Summary (1-2 sentences)

- Implemented an event-driven refresh mechanism for MCP gateways using the notifications send by the server to the client in mcp eg. `notifications/tools/list_changed` NOTE: notifications only work with long lived sessions, i.e with session pooling in gateway.
- Introduced a NotificationService that handles server notifications for pooled sessions, debounces rapid updates, and automatically triggers a gateway schema refresh (tools, resources, prompts) when changes are detected.

**NOTE:** _this same notifications service can be used for other notifications as well like **progress**, **cancellations**, etc. 
(gateway <->mcp server)_

---

## 🧪 Checks

- [x] `make lint` passes
- [x] `make test` passes
- [ ] CHANGELOG updated (if user-facing)

---

## 📓 Notes:

Architecture:

The implementation introduces a new NotificationService that acts as a bridge between the low-level MCPSessionPool and the high-level GatewayService.

1. Notification Handling: MCPSessionPool now configures ClientSession instances with a message handler that routes list_changed notifications to the NotificationService.
2. Debouncing: The service implements a configurable debounce mechanism (default 5s) to prevent "refresh storms" from chatty servers.
3. Context Propagation: Fixed a critical issue where gateway_id was not being propagated to pooled sessions, ensuring notifications can be correctly attributed to the source gateway. 
4. Automatic Refresh: The NotificationService holds a reference to GatewayService to trigger the existing _refresh_gateway_tools_resources_prompts logic efficiently.

Flow Diagram:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant MCP as MCP Server
    participant Pool as MCPSessionPool
    participant NS as NotificationService
    participant GS as GatewayService
    participant DB as Database

    Note over MCP, Pool: Session established with gateway_id context
    MCP->>Pool: notifications/tools/list_changed
    Pool->>NS: message_handler(notification)
    NS->>NS: Debounce (5s)
    NS->>GS: _refresh_gateway_tools_resources_prompts
    GS->>MCP: Call tool/list, resource/list, prompt/list
    MCP-->>GS: Return updated schemas
    GS->>DB: Sync changes (add/update/remove)
    Note right of GS: Updates reflected in database
```

Key Changes

1. New Service:  `mcpgateway/services/notification_service.py`
2. Session Pool: Updated `mcpgateway/services/mcp_session_pool.py` to auto-initialize notification handling and pass gateway_id.
3. Gateway Service: Updated `mcpgateway/services/gateway_service.py` to register capabilities (tools.listChanged support) and ensure health checks use gateway_id.
4. Tool/Resource Services: Updated tool_service.py and resource_service.py to pass gateway_id during session acquisition.
5. Main: Updated main.py to wire up the NotificationService startup.

Verification

- Added comprehensive unit tests for NotificationService.
- Verified end-to-end flow with a local MCP server triggering catalog updates.

---


## 🛠️ Testing:

1. Enable Session pooling in the gateway
```
MCP_SESSION_POOL_ENABLED=true
```

2. Run this MCP server, and add it in the context forge gateway
The server has two tools, simple `hello` tool and `add_dynamic_tool` tool that takes a tool name as input and when the tool is called with an input, it creates another tool with the name you passed as input and sends a `notifications/tools/list_changed` notification to the gateway.

```python
from fastmcp import FastMCP, Context

# Initialize with dependencies
mcp = FastMCP(name="dynamic-tools-mcp")

# -------------------------------------------------
# Initial tool
# -------------------------------------------------
@mcp.tool()
def hello(name: str) -> str:
    """Say hello."""
    return f"Hello {name}"

# -------------------------------------------------
# AdminMCP tool to add tools dynamically
# -------------------------------------------------
@mcp.tool()
async def add_dynamic_tool(tool_name: str, ctx: Context) -> str:
    """
    Adds a new tool at runtime and notifies clients.
    """
    # Define the new tool logic
    def dynamic_tool(text: str) -> str:
        return f"[{tool_name}] {text}"
    
    # Set the function name/metadata explicitly so FastMCP picks it up
    dynamic_tool.__name__ = tool_name
    dynamic_tool.__doc__ = f"Dynamically added tool '{tool_name}'"

    # Register the tool
    mcp.tool(name=tool_name)(dynamic_tool)

    # This sends the 'notifications/tools/list_changed' event
    await ctx.send_tool_list_changed()
    await ctx.info(f"Notification sent for new tool: {tool_name}")

    return f"Tool '{tool_name}' added successfully."

# -------------------------------------------------
# Run MCP server
# -------------------------------------------------
if __name__ == "__main__":
    mcp.run(transport="http", host="127.0.0.1", port=8001)
```

3. Once the server is added in the gateway, go to tools tabs, find add_dynamic_tool, click test tool.

4. Give input as `my_new_tool` and click Run Tool. Once executed the mcp server will automatically create a new tool inside the server and then will send a `notifications/tools/list_changed` notification to the gateway. The Gateway will read the notification, check for correct notification and will take the appropriate action and refresh/sync the server.

5. Reload the tools tab, check that the new tool: `my_new_tool` will be automatically show up in the tools list.

commits.message:
fix: address review feedback for notification service

Security & Correctness Fixes:
- Add per-gateway lock acquisition before calling _refresh_gateway_tools_resources_prompts
  to prevent race conditions with manual/auto refresh operations
- Implement flag merging during debounce window - subsequent notifications
  now merge their include_resources/include_prompts flags instead of being dropped
- Add tracking of pending refresh flags to support flag merging

Documentation:
- Update ADR-034 status from "Planned" to "Accepted"
- Document known limitation: session pool keys by URL/identity, not gateway_id,
  so multiple gateways sharing the same URL may have notification attribution issues
- Add limitation note to notification_service.py module docstring

Test Updates:
- Fix mock configuration for _get_refresh_lock (synchronous, returns asyncio.Lock)
- Add test for lock-held skip behavior
- Update e2e tests with proper lock mocking

Closes review feedback from PR #2071

Signed-off-by: Mihai Criveti <crivetimihai@gmail.com>

commits.message:
fix: add gateway_id to session pool key for correct notification attribution

Previously, session pool keys were (user_identity, url, identity_hash, transport_type).
If multiple gateways shared the same URL/auth, notifications would be attributed to
whichever gateway first created the session, causing the wrong gateway to be refreshed.

Changes:
- Add gateway_id as 5th element of PoolKey tuple
- Add gateway_id field to PooledSession dataclass
- Update _make_pool_key to include gateway_id parameter
- Update acquire/release to use gateway_id in pool key reconstruction
- Update _create_session to store gateway_id on PooledSession
- Update get_metrics to unpack 5-element pool key
- Add "Gateway Isolation" section to MCPSessionPool docstring
- Update ADR to note slightly reduced session reuse as trade-off
- Remove "Known Limitations" section since issue is now fixed
- Update all tests to use 5-element pool keys

The trade-off is slightly reduced session reuse when multiple gateways have
different gateway_ids but share the same URL/auth. This is acceptable because
correctness of notification attribution is more important than session reuse
efficiency for this edge case.

Signed-off-by: Mihai Criveti <crivetimihai@gmail.com>
